Rashi on Bava Kamma 35a:10:1.hebrew: דרך עלייה - שהרגו כלאחר יד בהרימו הגרזן, דקיימא לן (מכות דף ז:) דפטור מגלות, אפ"ה פטור מתשלומין. הלכך, גבי חילול שבת נמי, אפי' בשוגג פטור מלשלם:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 35a:10:1.english: By way of ascent - That he killed him indirectly while raising the axe — as we hold (Makkot 7b) that he is exempt from exile — even so, he is exempt from monetary payment. Therefore, regarding desecration of the Sabbath as well, even [when done] unintentionally, he is exempt from paying.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 35a:12:1.hebrew: ה"ג הכי קאמר כיון דבמזיד נידון בנפשו - והיכי דמי? בצריך לאפרו, השתא דשוגג פטור:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 35a:12:1.english: This is how we read [the text]: This is what it means: Since when [he acts] intentionally he is judged with his life - and what are the circumstances? When he needs its ashes; now that [he acted] unintentionally, he is exempt.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 35a:13:2.english: It was hurt by a rock - [It] was rubbing itself against a rock and was hurt.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 35a:14:1.english: Two [oxen] were pursuing one - And the three of them belong to three [different] people.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 35a:1:1.hebrew: אף הוא נמי דלא קבעי - לאפרו, ומקלקל הוא, וקתני פטור מתשלומין; אלמא חיוב מיתה איכא:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 35a:1:1.english: He too, where he does not need - its ashes, and he is [acting] destructively; and [yet] it teaches [that he is] exempt from payment — thus, there is liability to death.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 35a:2:1.hebrew: אף שורו דקבעי ליה - לאו דוקא, דאפי' לא בעי ליה נמי חייב לשלם, אלא על כרחיה תרוייהו בחדא מילתא מוקמינן — האי לחיובא והאי לפטורא — דהכי משמע מתני', דבמקום שזה חייב זה פטור. דאי שורו בלא קבעי ליה, לא מתורץ "יש חייב על מעשה שורו ופטור על מעשה עצמו", דהא איהו בדלא בעי ליה מחייב בתשלומין:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 35a:2:1.english: So too, his ox, where it needs [the ashes] - [This is] not meant strictly, for even if [the ox] does not need [the ashes], [the owner] is also liable to pay. Rather, perforce we establish both of them in the same situation — this one to liability and that one to exemption — for this is what the Mishnah implies, that in the [same] situation where this one is liable, that one is exempt. For if [the case of] his ox were where it does not need [the ashes], "[There are cases where one is] liable for the act of his ox and exempt for his own act" would not be explained, since he himself, when he does not need [the ashes], is liable for payment.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 35a:3:1.english: With an intelligent ox - That the ox is clever.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 35a:4:1.hebrew: ומנא ידעינן - דלהכי איכוין, דאצטריך לאשמועינן מתני' דאע"ג דמריה כי האי גוונא מפטר בתשלומין, הוי שור חייב; דאי מסתמא, אפי' מריה נמי מיחייב אי לא ידעינן ביה דצריך לאפרו, ואין כאן "יש חייב על מעשה שורו ופטור על מעשה עצמו":
Rashi on Bava Kamma 35a:4:1.english: And from where do we know - that it intended for this [purpose], such that the Mishnah needed to teach us that even though its owner in such a case is exempt from payment, the ox is liable; for if [it were] unspecified, even its owner would also be liable [to pay] if we did not know about it that it needed its ashes, and there would not be here [a case of] "there is one who is liable for the act of his ox and exempt for his own act."

Rashi on Bava Kamma 35a:5:2.english: And it pushed [off] the vat [cover] - [It] pushed the cover of the vessel in which the beer [was].

Rashi on Bava Kamma 35a:6:1.hebrew: שורו - דפטור דומיא דחיובא דידיה, היכי משכחת לה? הא חיובא דידיה ליתא אלא במתכוין לבייש, ושור אין בו דעת להתכוין לבושת:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 35a:6:1.english: His ox - [Where] he is exempt, similar to his [own] liability — how do you find it? For his [own] liability applies only when he intends to humiliate, and an ox has no mind to intend [to cause] humiliation.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 35a:7:1.hebrew: ומשני משכחת לה כגון שנתכוון השור להזיק - דגבי אדם כי האי גוונא מחייב אבושת, דאמר מר כו':
Rashi on Bava Kamma 35a:7:1.english: And [the Gemara] answers: You find it [in a case] where the ox intended to cause injury - For with regard to a person, in such a case he is liable for humiliation, as the Master said, etc.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 35a:8:1.hebrew: רבא אמר - לעולם מתני' בדלא קבעי ליה לאפרו, והאי דפטור מתשלומין לאו משום דליהוי ביה חיוב מיתה, דהא מתני' אפי' בשוגג נמי, דליכא חיוב מיתה, מיתוקמא דפטור מתשלומין, כדתני דבי חזקיה:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 35a:8:1.english: Rava said - Actually, the Mishnah [is referring to a case] where he does not need its ashes; and the reason he is exempt from payment is not because there is liability for the death penalty in it, for the Mishnah can be established even [in a case of] an unintentional [act] as well — where there is no liability for the death penalty — [such] that he is exempt from payment, as [the Tanna of] the school of Chizkiyah taught.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 35a:9:1.hebrew: מכה נפש בהמה ישלמנה ומכה אדם יומת - הוקשו יחד, דמה מכה בהמה לעולם משלם ואפי' בשוגג, כדאמרי' (לעיל בבא קמא דף כו.) אדם מועד לעולם — אף מכה אדם, דפטריה קרא מתשלומין דכתיב יומת, לעולם פטור ואפילו בשוגג, הואיל ובמזיד שייכא מיתה:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 35a:9:1.english: He who strikes the life of an animal shall pay for it, and he who strikes a man shall be put to death - They are juxtaposed together: for just as one who strikes an animal always pays, even [when acting] inadvertently — as we say (above, Bava Kamma 26a), "A person is always forewarned" — so too one who strikes a man, whom Scripture exempted from payment as it is written, "he shall be put to death," is always exempt, even [when acting] inadvertently, since when [done] intentionally, the death penalty applies.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 35a:10:1.hebrew: בין בשוגג בין במזיד - בג' ענייני ממון איירי תנא דבי חזקיה: בין בשוגג בין במזיד איירי בממון אחר בהדי מיתה, ונפקא לן מינה דחייבי מיתות שוגגים פטורים [מתשלומין] משום "דלא חלקת"; דאהכי מייתי לה בשמעתין ובאלו נערות (כתובות דף לה. ושם). ולענין זה אית להו לכ"ע הקישא דתנא דבי חזקיה, כדאמרינן בפ' אלו נערות: "ומי איכא למאן דלית להו דתנא דבי חזקיה". אבל בין מתכוון לשאינו מתכוון לאו בממון אחר בהדי מיתה איירי, דמקל וחומר משוגג נפקא, אלא לפטור מדמי הנהרג, לאפוקי מדרבי דדריש במתכוון להרוג זה והרג זה "ונתת נפש תחת נפש" — ממון; וקמ"ל תנא דבי חזקיה דכיון שנתכוון פטור, הכא נמי שאין מתכוון פטור, ואהכי מייתי לה בפרק הנשרפין (סנהדרין דף עט:). ובין דרך ירידה לדרך עלייה אתא: כמו דדרך עלייה לא ניתן שגגתו לכפרה, דלא שקלינן מיניה ממונא למפטריה, הכא נמי דרך ירידתו — אע"ג שניתנה שגגתו לכפרה — ולפטור מזיד אצטריך. ויש טועים לומר דלפטור שוגג דרך עלייה כמו דרך ירידה אצטריך; אבל בפרק אלו נערות (כתובות דף לה. ושם) בשמעתא ד"לא יהיה אסון" מוכיח סוגיא כדפרישית:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 35a:10:1.english: "Whether unintentionally or intentionally" - The school of Chizkiyah is speaking of three monetary matters: "Whether unintentionally or intentionally" speaks of another monetary [liability incurred] together with a capital [offense], and we derive from it that those liable to death who acted unintentionally are exempt [from payment] because "you do not differentiate"; for it is regarding this that [the Gemara] cites it in our sugya and in [the chapter] Eilu Na'arot (Ketubot 35a and there). And with regard to this matter, everyone agrees with the analogy of the school of Chizkiyah, as we say in the chapter Eilu Na'arot: "Is there anyone who does not hold [the teaching] of the school of Chizkiyah?" However, "whether advertently or inadvertently" does not speak of another monetary [liability] together with a capital [offense] — for that is derived by an a fortiori inference from an unintentional [killer] — rather, [it comes] to exempt [him] from the value of the slain person, to the exclusion of Rabbi [Yehudah HaNasi], who expounds regarding one who intended to kill this one and killed another: "Then you shall give a life for a life" — [meaning] monetary compensation; and the school of Chizkiyah teaches us that just as when he intended [to kill that person] he is exempt [from paying], so too when he did not intend [to kill him] he is exempt; and it is regarding this that [the Gemara] cites it in the chapter HaNisrafin (Sanhedrin 79b). And "whether by way of descent or by way of ascent" comes [to teach]: just as by way of ascent, its unintentional act is not given to atonement [through exile], as we do not take money from him to exempt him, so too by way of his descent — even though its unintentional act is given to atonement — and it is needed to exempt an intentional [killer]. And there are those who err and say that it is needed to exempt an unintentional [killer] by way of ascent, just like by way of descent; however, in the chapter Eilu Na'arot (Ketubot 35a and there), in the sugya of "there shall be no fatality," the sugya proves as I have explained.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 35a:2:1.hebrew: מה שורו דלא קבעי ליה - משמע דלא פריך אלא אליבא דר' יוחנן. ותימה, דלר' אבהו נמי תקשה: מה שורו דלא צריך לגופו כו'. ואם נאמר דרבי אבהו מחייב במקלקל גמור ולא בעי צריכה לגופה, א"ש:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 35a:2:1.english: Just as [in the case of] his ox, where he does not need it - This implies that [the Gemara] is only asking according to Rabbi Yochanan. And this is astonishing: according to Rabbi Abahu as well, it should be difficult: "Just as [in the case of] his ox, where [the act] is not needed for its own sake, etc." And if we say that Rabbi Abahu holds one liable [even] for a completely destructive act and does not require [that the act be] needed for its own sake, [then] it works out well.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 35a:6:1.hebrew: נתכוון לבייש היכי משכחת לה - תימה: כיון דלא אסיק אדעתיה "נתכוון להזיק", אפילו "הוא דומיא דשורו" נמי תקשה ליה, דבשור ליכא כוונה ובאדם בעי כוונה. וי"ל דאי אמרת "הוא דומיא דשורו", אז משמע שפיר כוונתו להזיק, ובא להשמיענו דלא בעינן כוונה לבייש אלא להזיק, דומיא דשורו. אבל "שור דומיא דידיה" משמע כוונה דשכיח טפי באדם מבשור, דהיינו כוונה דידיה לבייש, ואתא לאשמועינן שור דומיא דאדם דבעי' שיתכוין לבייש, דאילו מתכוון להזיק שכיח יותר בשור מבאדם. [ועוד] דליכא למימר דלהשמיענו דשור פטור במתכוין להזיק מבושת, דלהא לא אצטריך, דהא תנן בהחובל (לקמן בבא קמא דף פז.) דשור פטור בכל ארבעה דברים, וסתם שור הוא קרן שמתכוון להזיק. וא"כ ע"כ "שורו דומיא דידיה" שמתכוון לבייש, וזה א"א, ששור אין מתכוון לבייש; ועל כרחך אית לן למימר "הוא דומיא דשורו", וקמ"ל דלא בעינן מתכוון לבייש. ומשני: לעולם "שורו דומיא דידיה" שמתכוון, וקמ"ל שיכול להיות ששורו דומיא דידיה, וא"כ בדידיה לא בעינן שיתכוון לבייש, שזה אי אפשר להיות בשור:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 35a:6:1.english: How can you find [a case where the ox] intended to humiliate? - This is astonishing: Since [the Gemara] did not consider [the case of] "intended to injure," even [if it had said] "he is similar to his ox" it should also have asked against him, for in an ox there is no intention [to humiliate], whereas in a person intention is required! And one can answer that if you say "he is similar to his ox," then it implies well [that it refers to] his intention to injure, and it comes to teach us that we do not require intention to humiliate, rather [intention] to injure, similar to his ox. However, "an ox similar to him" implies an intention that is more common in a person than in an ox, namely his intention to humiliate, and it comes to teach us [that] an ox is similar to a person, in that we require that it intend to humiliate — whereas "intending to injure" is more common in an ox than in a person. [And furthermore,] one cannot say that [it comes] to teach us that an ox is exempt from humiliation when it intends to injure, for this is not needed, as we learned in [the chapter] HaChovel (later, Bava Kamma 87a) that an ox is exempt from all four [additional] payments, and an ordinary ox is [the category of] Horn, which intends to injure. And if so, perforce "his ox similar to him" [means] that it intends to humiliate, and this is impossible, for an ox does not intend to humiliate; so perforce we must say "he is similar to his ox," and it teaches us that we do not require intending to humiliate. And [the Gemara] answers: Actually, "his ox is similar to him" [means] that it intends [to injure], and it teaches us that it is possible for his ox to be similar to him, and if so, in his own case we do not require that he intend to humiliate, since this is impossible in an ox.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 35a:8:1.hebrew: מתניתין בשוגג - פי' בקונט' דרבא מוקי מתניתין דלא בעי לאפרו, ופטור מאותו טעם ששוגג פטור. ואין הלשון משמע כן; ועוד, דלא דמי לשוגג שיש בו איסור מלאכה, אבל כאן אין איסור מלאכה. אלא י"ל: "מתני' בשוגג", דבהא מלתא אשמועינן הוא דומיא דשורו: מה שורו בשוגג, אף הוא בשוגג, ואפילו הכי פטור מדתנא דבי חזקיה:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 35a:8:1.english: "The Mishnah [refers to] an unintentional [act]" - Rashi explained that Rava establishes our Mishnah [as a case] where he does not need its ashes, and he is exempt [from payment] for the same reason that an unintentional [offender on Shabbat] is exempt. However, the wording [of the Gemara] does not imply this; and furthermore, [such a case] is not comparable to an unintentional [act] where there is a prohibition of labor, whereas here there is no prohibition of labor. Rather, one should say: "[The Mishnah] refers to an unintentional [act]" — for in this matter, [the Mishnah] teaches us [that] "he" is similar to "his ox": just as his ox [acts] unintentionally, so too he [acts] unintentionally, and even so he is exempt because of [the teaching of] the school of Chizkiyah.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 35a:9:1.hebrew: מכה אדם ומכה בהמה - תימה, דבריש הנחנקין (סנהדרין דף פד:) מוקי האי קרא דתנא דבי חזקיה במכה אביו; ואע"ג דבמסקנא נפקא לן חבורה מאם אינו ענין לנפש בהמה, מ"מ מפיק מיניה התם דמותר להקיז דם לאביו, ומה שייך כאן לחלק בין דרך ירידה לדרך עלייה? וי"ל, דמיירי בין במכה אביו בין במכה חבירו: במכה אביו — מדכתיב הכאה סתם ולא כתיב "ומת", ובמכה חבירו — דבר הלמד מענינו, דומיא דקרא דלעיל מיניה "איש כי יכה כל נפש אדם", דמיירי ברוצח, כדמוכח בפרק יוצא דופן (נדה דף מד: ושם). ולצדדים מיירי: לענין חבירו במיתה, ולענין אביו בחבורה בעלמא; וכיון דבכולהו מיירי קרא, גמרינן שפיר ממכה בהמה:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 35a:9:1.english: One who strikes a man and one who strikes an animal - [This is] astonishing, for at the beginning of [the chapter] HaNechnakin (Sanhedrin 84b), [the Gemara] establishes this verse of the school of Chizkiyah as [referring to] one who strikes his father; and even though in the conclusion we derive [the prohibition of causing] a wound from [the principle] "if it has no application to [striking] the life of an animal," nevertheless [the Gemara] derives from it there that it is permitted to let blood for one's father — so what relevance is there here to distinguish between a downward motion and an upward motion? And one can say that [the verse] refers both to one who strikes his father and to one who strikes his fellow: [it refers] to one who strikes his father, since "striking" is written unspecified and it is not written "and he dies"; and [it refers] to one who strikes his fellow [by the principle of] a matter learned from its context, similar to the verse preceding it, "And a man who strikes any human life" (Leviticus 24:17), which refers to a murderer, as is proven in the chapter Yotzei Dofen (Niddah 44b and there). Thus it refers [to them] separately: regarding his fellow, with [the death penalty for] killing, and regarding his father, with a mere wound; and since the verse refers to all of them, we properly derive [our law] from "one who strikes an animal."
